page: Microsoft Azure L48s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by a 24-core, 48-vCPU Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture with hyper-threading enabled and capable of reaching clock frequencies up to 4.2 GHz. The hardware platform includes 260 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. System memory totals 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, and operates without discrete hardware GPU acceleration.

High-throughput local persistence is provided by 11520 GB of integrated NVMe SSD capacity, configured for I/O-intensive operation. Synthetic performance indicators show high read memory bandwidth reaching 223.94 GB/sec on large 256MB blocks, alongside strong Geekbench scores of 2161 for single-core and 20273 for multi-core execution. PassMark evaluation yielded a total CPU score of 63100.84 and a database operations mark of 25789.77. In-memory data structures demonstrated throughput of 67.33 million operations per second during Redis SET benchmarks, while multithreaded compression and decompression workloads maintained sustained performance.

The resource profile of the L48s_v4 offers strong cost efficiency for platforms that demand co-located large storage and memory footprints, eliminating external network disk overheads. However, workloads requiring hardware graphic or matrix accelerator pipelines will experience limits due to the absence of dedicated GPUs. The instance is structured for distributed databases, high-capacity caching nodes, static web delivery infrastructure, and large transactional data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure L48s_v4 is a storage-optimized instance configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with 260 MB of L3 cache, it supports AVX-512 and AMX extensions under Microsoft Hyper-V. Memory capacity stands at 384.0 GB, paired with 11520 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and zero discrete GPUs. Performance tests show strong results, including 67.33 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, a PassMark CPU score of 63100.84, and high-volume data compression capability. By packaging 11.5 TB of NVMe SSD directly into the compute instance, the platform delivers high qualitative cost efficiency for data-heavy tiers, avoiding network storage latency. It is targeted at transactional databases, large caching layers, search indexing, and real-time analytical query workloads.
